as_read: Mixed: positive for low back pain at a stated salicin dose (10936472, moderate quality per Cochrane 25536022), conflicting in osteoarthritis (11406860, 15517622), and the labels print extract mass without salicin in the rows.

studies_to_add.quote: The principal outcome measure was the proportion of patients who were pain-free without tramadol for at least 5 days during the final week of the study.

studies_to_add.quote: The OA study suggested that the willow bark extract showed no relevant efficacy in patients with OA.

stop_list: Fields can't express a salicin-equivalent dose against labels that print only extract or powder mass. Salicin values in the packet doses are salicin mg, not extract mass.
labels.py rows show no salicin; the label panels themselves weren't opened.
clinician_items: 10936472: one patient suffered a severe allergic reaction, perhaps to the extract.

11345689: at 240 mg salicin/day, maximal platelet aggregation differed from placebo with arachidonic acid (p = 0.04) and ADP (p = 0.01), to a far lesser extent than acetylsalicylate; the authors ask whether this matters in patients with impaired thrombocyte function.
stored_rating_note: Stored positive_strong rests on one low back pain trial. 15517622 is null in osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis, and 37895439 calls certainty inadequate. The stored population text covers musculoskeletal discomfort, broader than the stored trial. mixed fits better; positive holds for low back pain alone.
unread_notes: Abstracts only. One search used (41 hits).
